summary: Maalyada Konduparti is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She was a visiting faculty member at Andhra University in 2015, an assistant professor at Alliance University (2016-2017) and REVA University (2017-2021), and became associate professor at GITAM University in 2021.
Maanasa Visweswaran is a scholar in Indology and computational studies. In 2026, she is attested as studying and serving as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg.

Mabel Haynes Bode was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a Ph.D. at Bern (1898) and studied under scholars including Rhys Davids and Sylvain Lévi. She taught at University College London (1909-1917) and SOAS (1917).

Madan Mohan Malaviya was an Indologist educated at Muir Central College, the University of Calcutta (B.A.), and the University of Allahabad (LL.B., 1891). He taught at Government Inter College, Prayagraj, and founded Banaras Hindu University, serving as vice-chancellor (1919-1938).

Madeleine Biardeau (1922-2010) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the ENS de Sèvres, the University of Kerala, and under K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri, later serving as professor at EPHE (circa 1956-1989).

Madeleine Giteau was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning degrees from the EPHE and Sorbonne Nouvelle, she worked at the National Museum of Cambodia, taught at Royal University of Phnom Penh, and was affiliated with EFEO and Sorbonne Nouvelle.

Madeleine Hallade was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist and Central Asian studies. She studied at the ENSBA and École du Louvre under Joseph Hackin and Moritz Abraham Stern, later serving at the Guimet Museum and École du Louvre.
Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He held a professorship at the University of Michigan, with posts attested in 1976, 1997, and 2006 to 2009.

Madhav Sadashiv Gore (1921-2010) studied at the University of Mumbai, under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye, and at the Columbia University School of Social Work. He later held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (circa 1982-1987).

Madhu Khanna is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford. In 2012, she is attested holding posts at Jamia Millia Islamia as director and at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Madhu Parameswaran works in Indology. He earned an MD in Dravyagunavijnan from Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (2007-2010) and served at Vaidyaratnam P.S. Varier Ayurveda College as assistant professor in 2011, with affiliation attested in 2021.
Madhura Balasubramaniam works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She was a project associate (2018-2020) at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras, where she earned her PhD in 2022.

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who graduated from Fergusson College. He founded the Archeology Research Group in Porbandar (1951) and was associate director and director emeritus of research at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Madhusudan Gupta was an Indologist who studied at Sanskrit College and University and Calcutta Medical College. He taught Ayurveda at Sanskrit College (circa 1830-1835) and later served at Calcutta Medical College (circa 1835-1856).
Madhusudan Kaul Shastri was an Indology scholar who served as Superintendent of the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir, attested between 1918-1934 and 1943-1945.
Madhusudan Rimal is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Alberta in 2016 and held an attested post there in 2021.
Madhusudan Singh Vats (1896-1972) was an Indian scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Rakhal Das Banerji (Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay).

Magdalena Szpindler specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned degrees from the University of Warsaw (M.A., 2004) and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (doctor, 2022), serving as adiunkt at the University of Warsaw in 2019.

Magdalene Geiger was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (1911) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1915), under Hermann Beckh, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Geiger.

Magdalene Sophie Schott was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the universities of Tübingen, Münster, Berlin, Freiburg, and Marburg, completing her Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (1928-1935) under Max Walleser.
